title: Connection & context: The variable neural architecture of social relationships
title_zh: 连接与情境：社会关系的可变神经架构
abstract: Our brains are contextual, connected, social, and dynamic; failing to account for these aspects of the brain together risks misleading results that could be translated into worse health outcomes, especially for populations already underrepresented in neuroscience. In this manuscript, we synthesize recent studies that investigate the network neuroecology of social interaction and characterize how brain network organization varies across interpersonal social experience. We describe how certain patterns of brain connectivity are associated with particular social environments as a result of trade-offs in how functional connections are distributed across the brain in accordance with social experience. We call these environment-specific patterns of connectivity and their trajectories of reconfiguration over development network neuroendophenotypes. We propose two intersecting mechanisms that underlie the development of network neuroendophenotypes, addressing both how and why brain network organization contextually varies: one more protracted via stress physiology and the other more acute via the processing of affective/supportive touch. The existence of distinguishable patterns of connectivity that are associated with different social environments has important consequences for studying normative neurodevelopment and brain-based biomarkers of disease: The pattern of brain network organization that is associated with better (mental) health may look different in different environments. Ignoring social context therefore risks either pathologizing healthy brains or dismissing real disease among those who would otherwise be considered healthy. Moving forward, methodological advances that can effectively treat brain network organization as a dynamic, high dimensional, contextually influenced neuroendophenotype will be crucial for future research.
abstract_zh: 我们的脑部是情境化、互联、社会化且动态的；若未能同时考虑这些脑部特性，可能导致误导性结果，并在已被低估的神经科学人群中转化为更差的健康结果。在本文中，我们综合了近期研究，探讨社会互动的网络神经生态，并描述脑网络组织如何随人际社会经验而变化。我们阐述了某些脑连接模式如何因功能连接在大脑中按社会经验分布的权衡而与特定社会环境相关联。我们将这些环境特定的连接模式及其随发展重构的轨迹称为网络神经表型。我们提出两种交叉机制，解释网络神经表型的发展，既涉及通过应激生理的更长期过程，也涉及通过情感/支持性触摸处理的更急性过程。存在与不同社会环境相关的可区分连接模式，对研究规范性神经发育和基于脑的疾病生物标志物具有重要意义：与更好（心理）健康相关的脑网络组织模式在不同环境中可能呈现不同。忽视社会情境因此可能导致将健康大脑病理化，或忽视本应被视为健康者的真实疾病。未来，能够有效将脑网络组织视为动态、高维、受情境影响的神经表型的方法学进步，对后续研究至关重要。
